commit.message: Send reviews to the team's tracker (0.7.1)

findings.title: Top-level async IIFE has no catch, so failures skip restore() and cleanup
findings.description: Everything runs inside `(async () => { ... })()` with no `.catch()`. Any throw between `install(vscode)` at line 57 and `restore()` at line 118 leaves the vscode stub globally installed and skips the exit-code summary; the temp repo created at line 42 is never removed on any path. Since this test drives a real commit and a real POST, a mid-run failure is a likely case rather than a rare one.
findings.suggestion: Consider wrapping the body in try/finally that always calls `restore()`, removes the temp repo, and exiting via a `.catch()` that prints the error and sets a non-zero code.

findings.title: last-review.json is read unguarded after checks that tolerate a failed review
findings.description: The checks at lines 92-99 are written to fail gracefully when the review times out or delivery is rejected, but line 101 then reads `.cr-track/last-review.json` unconditionally. On any of those failure paths the file may not exist, so `readFileSync` throws: the four remaining payload checks never run, `restore()` and the summary at 118-119 are skipped, and the run dies as an unhandled rejection instead of printing `N passed / M failed`.
findings.suggestion: Consider guarding the read (e.g. `fs.existsSync(...)` and otherwise recording it as a failed check) so a failed review still produces a readable summary and restores the stub.

findings.title: Endpoint property is dereferenced before the check that it exists
findings.description: `prop.default` and `prop.description` are read at lines 1121-1126, but the check that `crTrack.endpoint` exists at all only runs afterwards at 1129-1130. If the property is ever dropped from package.json, `prop` is undefined and the TypeError aborts the whole suite before the check that was meant to report exactly that failure. The new block also introduces a bare `{ ... }` scope whose indentation no longer matches the surrounding checks.
findings.suggestion: Consider hoisting the existence check above the reads and using optional chaining, so a missing property reports as a failed check rather than crashing the run.

findings.title: Activation check passes when the status bar was never written
findings.description: Activation is asserted as "the status text does not contain ` · `", which is also true when `state.statusText` is empty or undefined — i.e. when the extension failed to set it at all. The check would then pass on exactly the failure it is guarding against.
findings.suggestion: Consider asserting something positive as well, e.g. that `state.statusText` is a non-empty string that does not contain the error separator.

findings.title: Findings are formatted before the check that their fields exist
findings.description: `f.severity.padEnd(10)` at line 108 runs before the check at 111-113 that verifies every finding actually carries `severity`. A finding missing that field throws here, so the assertion designed to report the problem never executes.
findings.suggestion: Consider defaulting the field for display, e.g. `String(f.severity ?? "?").padEnd(10)`, so the check at line 111 is what reports a malformed payload.
